name: PageCurlMeshBuilder
src_typeComment: The shared curl-deformation math used by both the UI (PageCurlGraphic) and 3D (PageCurlMeshRenderer) adapters, so the two contexts never drift out of sync with two copies of the same formula.  This is a SIMPLIFIED single-axis roll, not a full two-corner-drag curl: the fold line always runs parallel to the hinge edge (it doesn't tilt toward wherever the page was grabbed vertically), so curlProgress is the only input needed. It still reads as a convincing rolling-cylinder page turn with self-shadowing — just without the extra asymmetric skew of a full corner-drag curl. Always builds in a canonical space: hinge at localX = 0, free edge (where the user grabs to turn the page) at localX = width. Callers that need the opposite hinge side (e.g. a book's left page) mirror the surface's own Transform (localScale.x = -1) rather than baking mirroring into this math, so triangle winding here never needs to account for it.  THE SHAPE OF A TURN. A page being turned has three regions at any moment, in order along the page: 1. the FLAT part still lying on the near side, from the hinge out to the fold line; 2. the ROLLED part, wrapped around a cylinder sitting on the fold line; 3. the RETURNED part, which has come over the top of that cylinder and lies flat on the FAR side, upside down, at twice the cylinder's radius above the page. Region 3 is what makes a turn actually finish. An earlier version of this file derived the cylinder radius as rollDistance / PI, which forces the rolled part to wrap EXACTLY half a circle no matter how far the turn has progressed — so region 3 could never exist, and at curlProgress = 1 the page was a half-cylinder standing upright on the hinge (free edge at x = 0, but 2 * width / PI ABOVE the page) instead of lying flat on the far side. That is the "only curls halfway" bug, and because the book then hid the curl surface at the end of the turn, the standing tube also popped out of existence.  The radius is instead driven by a sine over the turn, so it opens from nothing, is widest mid-turn, and closes back to nothing — which lands the page exactly flat and mirrored at curlProgress = 1, precisely on top of the static backing page that replaces it. That coincidence is the whole point: the handoff at the end of a turn becomes invisible.

src_members.name: MaxRollRadiusFraction
src_members.comment: Widest cylinder radius mid-turn, as a fraction of page width. Bigger = a looser, fatter roll that lifts further off the page; smaller = a tighter curl closer to a hard crease. 0.16 reads as paper.

src_members.sig: public static PageMeshData Allocate(int columns, int rows)
src_members.name: Allocate
src_members.comment: Allocates a PageMeshData sized for the given grid. Call ONCE (e.g. in Awake/constructor) and reuse it via the Build(ref) overload below — the curl surface's mesh is rebuilt every frame during any active drag or turn-settle animation, so allocating fresh arrays each time is real, avoidable GC pressure. The one-shot Build() overload further below still allocates fresh each call, for simple one-off callers (self-tests, tools that only need a single static mesh) that don't need this.

src_members.id: Build(float, float, int, int, float, float, ref PageMeshData)
src_members.sig: public static void Build(float width, float height, int columns, int rows, float curlProgress, float shadowDarkness, ref PageMeshData data)
src_members.name: Build
src_members.comment: width/height: page size in local units. columns/rows: grid density (higher = smoother curl, more triangles) — MUST match what `data` was Allocate()'d with. curlProgress: 0 = flat page, 1 = fully turned over, lying flat and mirrored on the far side of the hinge (x running 0 to -width). shadowDarkness: brightness multiplier (0-1) applied to the page's underside once it rolls past the halfway point, for a cheap self-shadow look without needing real lighting. Fills `data`'s arrays in place — no allocation, safe to call every frame.

src_members.id: Build(float, float, int, int, float, float)
src_members.sig: public static PageMeshData Build(float width, float height, int columns, int rows, float curlProgress, float shadowDarkness)
src_members.name: Build
src_members.comment: Convenience one-shot overload — allocates a fresh PageMeshData every call. Fine for a self-test or any caller that only builds a mesh once; anything that rebuilds every frame (dragging, turn animation) should Allocate() once and reuse the Build(ref) overload above instead.
